briefing.headline: Two Boston-local shots and one perfect marketing-analytics hybrid are today's real prizes — the keyword score buried all three.
briefing.focus: Spend today's 20 minutes on the roles that sit exactly at the intersection of your two lanes AND clear the sponsorship bar: Twilio's Marketing Analyst (PLG analytics, remote-US, public co) and Amazon's AWS Marketing IDC Business Analyst are literally 'marketing funnel analyst' jobs — your SQL/Tableau/attribution stack maps 1:1. Then hit the Boston-local pair: AWS Storage PMM (Boston-based req at the largest H-1B sponsor in the US) and CarGurus B2B Marketing Specialist (right level, right city, public company). Skip the fit-100 roles from Gusto/Front/Verkada — they scored high on keywords but are SF-onsite, sponsorship-shaky, or off-lane.

ranked.why: Marketing analyst on funnel/PLG data — your two lanes in one title, remote-US, and Twilio is an established sponsor; scored only 91 because of three trivial missing keywords.
A Boston-based PMM req at the #1 H-1B sponsor in the country — location, lane, and visa all solved at once; the 88 score badly undersells it.
Demand-gen measurement frameworks and campaign dashboards — this is your marketing-funnel analytics work with Amazon's sponsorship machine behind it.
Boston HQ, NASDAQ-listed, 'Specialist' level matches your non-senior target, and it's B2B marketing — the strongest local-lane fit on the board.
'Associate' marketing automation manager at a public company — your Eloqua/HubSpot ops background at exactly the right level, and Yext sponsors.
Associate-level GTM ops at Datadog — big reliable sponsor, Boston office exists, and the title won't screen you out for seniority.
Paid LinkedIn ownership with efficiency metrics — pure demand gen at associate level; the 88 score missed how cleanly your funnel/attribution work maps.
Customer stories and case studies are literally on your skills list, and Datadog is a dependable sponsor with a Boston presence.
Amazon Business is B2B procurement — the only Amazon PMM req where your six years of B2B positioning is the direct qualification.
ABM is your headline skill and this is the non-senior version of the AWS ABM reqs; strong sponsorship, East Coast (Arlington).
Boston analyst role at a real mid-size company — clean lane-2 fit; verify sponsorship early since SimpliSafe is PE-owned and smaller.
Remote-US lifecycle marketing at Stripe Capital — your banking/fintech domain is a genuine differentiator here, not a nice-to-have.
GTM analytics, remote-US, and the ATS score is real — but Lattice is mid-size private, so sponsorship is the open question, not fit.
Posted today, MongoDB is a heavy and consistent H-1B sponsor, and lifecycle/PLG growth is squarely in your funnel wheelhouse.
'Audience and Messaging' is positioning and segmentation by another name — your exact craft, at a public company that sponsors.
Second Boston CarGurus req at the right level — brand is a step off your B2B core, but proximity and company quality carry it.
Waltham, MA at a public GTM-data company — the 61 score is a keyword artifact; ZoomInfo's whole product is the funnel you already run.
US-wide location, Stripe sponsors, and commerce/payments GTM is where your fintech years actually count.
Near-duplicate of the Datadog GTM ops associate req — apply to both, the teams post separately and screen separately.
ABX is ABM — your top skill in the title, at one of the most reliable H-1B sponsors; the 60 score is just an empty JD.
'Specialist' level B2B performance marketing at Adobe — huge sponsor, correct seniority; the low fit score is missing-JD noise, not a real signal.
AMZ-numbered reqs are the postings Amazon runs through immigration channels — the most sponsorship-transparent analyst role here, and BA II is your level.
Boston HQ, public, and Salesforce/GTM systems overlap your stack — but it's a product-owner role, so you're arguing adjacency.
US-Remote GTM planning at Stripe — fintech domain plus your funnel-metrics fluency; program-manager framing keeps it non-senior.
Straightforward lane-2 analyst req at Amazon posted yesterday — no marketing angle, but sponsorship and volume make it a high-odds application.
Marketing ops strategy is a real lane match at a public company; SF-onsite is the cost and the 'strategy partner to leadership' framing runs senior.
Partner/ISV demand gen at AWS — good sponsorship and pipeline work, but partner marketing is a sidestep from your product-marketing core.
ABM plus partner marketing at AWS; solid on paper, but you're competing against internal partner-marketing lifers.
Demand gen is your core skill and it's fully remote-US, but Grafana is smaller and remote-first companies are inconsistent on sponsorship.
Public company and a legitimate GTM ops fit, but 'Remote - Houston' usually means a real geographic tie, not open remote.
6sense sells ABM, so your ABM background reads as native — but it's a mid-size private firm and remote reqs there rarely carry sponsorship.
Braze is martech adjacent to your Eloqua/HubSpot experience and public, but technology-partner PMM is a narrow, relationship-heavy slice.
Anthropic sponsors and the brand is a career accelerator, but field marketing is SF/NYC onsite and the applicant pool is brutal.
Scored 100 on keywords but it's health-insurance sales operations, not marketing — wrong function dressed in the right words.
Fit 100 is misleading: SF-onsite, mid-size private, and the req is missing four of your strongest signals (attribution, segmentation, experimentation).
Perfect keyword match, weak real match — San Mateo onsite-heavy culture and no sponsorship signal make this a poor use of a slot.
Kubernetes/GPU infrastructure PMM demands deep technical depth your fintech background doesn't supply; the 97 score read tooling, not domain.
